An AI just read a stranger's mind through their skull, no surgery, no implants, and got roughly 45% of the meaning right on the first try. On a person it had never seen before.

That's the tech an OpenAI researcher just quit her job for. Two weeks ago she walked out of the hottest company on earth to join Conduit, a startup collecting brain recordings in a San Francisco basement.

Her timeline says developers wear thought-streaming headbands by 2027. By 2035, AI stops feeling like a tool and starts feeling like a limb.

content:
Massive breakthrough here!

Self-hosting LLMs just got ~75% cheaper:

Most agent pipelines now run 4-5 small models under the hood: an embedder for retrieval, a reranker for precision, an extractor for entities, and often a small LLM for routine generation.

The standard way to serve them is one server per model. vLLM holds the LLM, TEI holds the embedder, and everything else gets a custom FastAPI wrapper.

Each server reserves its own slice of GPU memory and holds it whether traffic arrives or not. GPUs are billed by the hour, so idle time costs the same as busy time.

This is why switching to small models rarely reduces the bill. The cost was never in the calls but rather in the servers.

The structural fix is serving every model from one process that loads and evicts models based on traffic.

Superlinked just open-sourced exactly that. SIE (Superlinked Inference Engine) is an Apache 2.0 server that runs 85+ models behind one API.

Four calls cover the whole pipeline:
- encode() returns vectors
- score() returns relevance scores
- extract() returns entity spans
- and generate() runs small open LLMs.

Models load on first request and are evicted least-recently-used, so one GPU serves a rotating set of models instead of sitting siloed behind one.

It runs anywhere from a laptop to a Kubernetes cluster, and it plugs into Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, LanceDB, LangChain, and LlamaIndex.

You can find the repo here: https://t.co/zK4Dk7418f

(don't forget to star 🌟)

I also wrote a hands-on guide to using SIE. It walks through a real-world example where we deploy and manage five models on a single GPU, including a small language model, an OCR model, an NER model, a reranker, and an object detector.

The article is quoted below.

content:
Cloudflare built a browser that runs INSIDE a Cloudflare Worker 🤯

Cloudflare Agents Week day 4 is here, and it's a banger:

🪁 Kitesurf: agent-first browser running on Workers
🕸️ WebMCP: Give any website an MCP interface
⚒️ The next generation of MCP is here
🔍 AI Search improvements + pricing announced
🤖 AI Readiness in the Dash & AEO diagnosis
🌎 Building an open Agentic Internet

🪁 Kitesurf: agent-first browser running on Workers 🪁

There are projects that come up from time to time that are uniquely Cloudflare, and Kitesurf is one of them. Workers are an insanely powerful primitive, and there is very little they can't do these days.

Kitesurf is a browser built for the agentic web. Chromium-backed browsers are large, and use a lot of memory. There simply isn't enough memory for every agent in the world to have a browser. That's where Kitesurf comes in, a lightweight alternative to Chromium-based browsers.

It uses WebAssembly, Dynamic Workers, Durable Objects and more to make this happen. And yes, it can run Doom.

Best of all, it's available in open beta to try today for free, via Browser Rendering's CDP endpoint and Quick Actions.

If you want to see it in action, there's a public playground too, linked below, as well as the full blog post - which is packed with interesting technical details!

🕸️ WebMCP: Give any website an MCP interface 🕸️

WebMCP is a new browser standard that lets any website expose itself via MCP. Rather than an agent having to click around the website, it can interact with it using MCP instead.

You could implement this yourself, but why would you, when Cloudflare can enable it on your site with one toggle?

You can enable this in the dashboard today under Agent Readiness > Labs. There's currently two groups of featuers you can enable, called packs, to help agents browser your website.

⚒️ The next generation of MCP is here ⚒️

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has evolved over time, and the latest iteration makes it simpler than ever. How? By making it so that an MCP server can be stateless. That removes the burden of sticky sessions and other complexities from running an MCP server.

With the rapid movement of the AI landscape, it's important for companies to move in the direction the puck is going. Once again, Cloudflare is ready to receive the puck, as stateless MCP servers have been possible on Cloudflare for some time.

That means, from day one of the specification being announced, it has been supported on Cloudflare when using the official MCP SDKs.

There's a bunch of other changes as part of this spec, including:

- Elicitation no longer needs an open stream
- Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name in HTTP headers, to avoid parsing request bodies for features such as rate limiting
- MCP now prefers pre-registered clients when the server and client already have a relationship, then Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) for dynamic registrations, with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) as a fallback

And much more. This is a good one to read yourself, as there's a lot of technical depth to the article!

🔍 AI Search Improvements 🔍

AI Search is Cloudflare's offering to solve the problem of how you give your AI agent access to specific knowledge to improve its work. In simple terms, it makes the RAG aspect of your AI agents effortless.

AI Search already lets you ingest data into an R2 bucket, scrape your own website, along with an array of options at search time.

AI search can now:

- You no longer need a sitemap to ingest your website's data, Cloudflare will discover the pages automatically
- Get a single public endpoint for searching across a namespace (both /search and /mcp).
- Add a custom domain to your public AI search namespaces
- Add semantic search to your sites built on EmDash (Cloudflare's WordPress successor) with AI Search plugin

AI Search always identifies itself when crawling websites, and respects bot protections that website owners put in place.

Pricing is also being announced today, as AI Search has been in beta since its release. As always, there's a generous free plan too, with full details in the blog post.

🤖 AI Readiness in the Dash & AEO diagnosis  Share of Voice

Getting your website ready for the agentic era is no small feat. There's a ton of protocols, and a bunch of considerations around how to make your website accessible to AI agents.

In April, Cloudflare launched a tool to check your website's readiness for AI agents. That tool is now available in the dashboard for all your websites hosted on Cloudflare.

Alongside the check, the tool provides actionable insights on how to improve your website's agent readiness.

Now, if you thought getting your website ready for agents was some dark art, then AEO takes that to another level.

AEO is the practise of getting your website content surfaced in public LLMs such as ChatGPT and Gemini.

Working out if your website is AEO optimised is incredibly hard. That's why Cloudflare is launching a new tool today that allows you to get insights into how your website performs on the AEO front, with insights such as:

- Citation Rate
- Prominence
- Mention Rate
- Share of Voice

Putting your website behind Cloudflare has always been a no-brainer, but it's rapidly becoming a deal breaker with the new tools available to websites hosted on Cloudflare, such as the new AEO tool.

🌎 Building an open Agentic Internet 🌎

AI agents are a new kind of web user, they are already overtaking humans in terms of request volume.

Every request has a paying human behind it, so if you treat agents the same way you do web scrapers, you're potentially blocking paying customers.

That's why Cloudflare is working hard to set the standards to make the web ready for the agentic era. These are based on open standards such as x402, MCP, Web Bot Auth and PACT.

There's four pillars that Cloudflare believes paves the way for an Agentic web:

- Readable, so agents can read content cheaply via Markdown (and Kitesurf, a lightweight agent-first browser!)
- Discoverable, meaning agents can find things through AI Search, and sites measure their agent visibility with AEO
- Callable, with sites exposing actions directly to agents via WebMCP and Code Mode
- Payable, with agents paying per use with Wallets and x402. Monetization Gateway lets sites charge agents in a few clicks, replacing broken ad models of what came before.

Ultimately, Cloudflare's mission is to help build a better Internet. Today, it is reaffirming that aim in the era of the agentic web, with the aim to enable AI agents and website owners to thrive on the agentic internet.

If you made it this far, thank you for reading - it was a pretty chonky one today, and there's one more day of announcements tomorrow! What did you think of today's announcements?

It will be defined by who owns the intelligence, who controls the infrastructure, and who benefits from the value it creates. Today, much of the AI economy is concentrated within a handful of companies that control the models, the data, and the computing resources. Decentralized AI introduces a framework where ownership and governance can be shared across global communities. This shift has the potential to make innovation more open, transparent, and economically inclusive.

Blockchain gives decentralized AI something that traditional architectures struggle to achieve, which is programmable trust @quipnetwork . Every contribution to an AI network can be recorded, verified, and rewarded without depending on centralized intermediaries. Whether someone provides computing power, high quality datasets, model improvements, or security validation, blockchain creates a transparent system for recognizing those contributions. This strengthens collaboration because participants know their efforts can be measured fairly. Trust becomes embedded in the network itself rather than delegated to a single institution.

The combination of crypto and AI also creates a new economic model where intelligent agents can operate independently. Instead of requiring constant human supervision, AI agents can interact with decentralized applications, execute transactions, manage digital assets, and coordinate workflows across blockchain networks. Smart contracts provide predictable execution while AI contributes adaptive reasoning and decision making. Together they enable systems capable of responding dynamically to changing conditions without sacrificing transparency. This represents a major step toward autonomous digital economies.

Privacy will remain one of the defining challenges as AI adoption accelerates. Users increasingly want powerful intelligent systems without giving up complete control over their personal information @TheARCTERMINAL . Decentralized AI supported by cryptographic technologies offers a path toward balancing innovation with privacy. Secure computation, encryption, and user controlled identities allow intelligence to operate while respecting ownership of sensitive data. This balance will become increasingly important as AI expands into finance, healthcare, education, and other critical sectors.

Community participation is another reason decentralized AI continues to gain momentum. Open ecosystems allow developers, researchers, node operators, and users from around the world to contribute to shared infrastructure instead of relying on a single organization. Diverse contributions often lead to more resilient models and faster innovation because ideas come from a broader range of perspectives. Incentive mechanisms encourage continuous improvement while strengthening long term sustainability. The result is an ecosystem where growth benefits everyone who helps build it.

Crypto and decentralized AI are laying the foundation for a more open digital future where intelligence is no longer controlled by a few centralized platforms. Blockchain provides ownership, transparency, and economic coordination, while AI delivers automation, reasoning, and continuous learning. Together they create systems that are not only more capable but also more accountable and inclusive @NucleusCodes . content:
Stop optimizing tokens. Index your context instead!

Retrieval quality is the foundation of context engineering. Karpathy described it best: the heavy cognitive work should happen at ingestion, not at query time. When knowledge is properly structured before retrieval, the model's job becomes reasoning, not sorting.

Most AI systems focus on compressing what the model sees. The more important problem is what gets retrieved before the model sees anything.

Token efficiency starts at retrieval. When context is properly indexed and prepared, the model spends its tokens on reasoning. When retrieval is weak, the model spends those same tokens sorting through noise and filling gaps from its own weights.

That's the silent failure mode. Retrieval returns topically correct but incomplete context. The model completes the gaps from parametric knowledge and streams it out the same way as grounded content. No signal in the output tells you which parts came from retrieved context and which came from weights. The answer looks confident. It just isn't complete.

The common assumption is that hallucination is the main failure mode. It's not. Models handle off-domain questions reasonably well now. If nothing in the retrieved context looks relevant, there's no material to build an answer on. The harder failure is partial coverage. The right document was retrieved. But not the full picture.

Coverage gaps don't produce error messages. They produce confident answers with pieces missing.

This gets worse when sources stay isolated. The same person might appear across multiple tools and systems. If those sources are indexed separately, the model has to figure out they refer to the same entity on its own. That's work that should happen before the model starts reasoning.

Glean's system of context is built around this problem:

• Unified index across all connected applications, not each source kept separate
• Specialized indexes for different types of information: company data, code, experts, profiles, tools, and calendars
• Multiple retrieval methods - semantic when meaning matters, lexical when exact terms matter, structured when fields and relationships need to stay intact
• Enterprise Graph that maps relationships across people, teams, customers, and projects so relevance reflects how the company actually works
• Memory that carries context forward across sessions and tasks
• Tools that let the model act on what it finds

The gap between finding information and understanding it is where most AI systems fall short.

content:
Jeffrey Ladish, Executive Director of Palisade Research, on why the people building AI are more frightened by it than the people criticizing it from outside:

"I think the scariest thing I hear from people working inside of the companies is that they think they are on the way to recursive self-improvement."

He explains what that actually means, the moment AI stops needing humans in the loop of its own development:

"The point where AI agents are writing all of the code and doing all of the research for the next generation of AI agents. You have really smart AI making smarter AI making smarter AI and so on. And that's a runaway process potentially."

And according to the people closest to it, this isn't a distant hypothetical:

"They think that they're going to be able to do it. They're like we are not that many years, maybe one, maybe two, maybe three years from that process happening. That terrifies me."

Asked what the repercussions of that could be, Ladish reaches for a comparison to a different kind of species-level discontinuity:

"It's a little bit like asking, what are the repercussions of homo sapiens coming on the scene in a world of monkeys and apes? How are the chimpanzees opposed to forecast what will happen to the whole Earth once you have a species that can use tools and language and fire and build skyscrapers."

He continues, making clear this isn't confined to chatbots on a screen:

"I do not know what AI agents that are a lot smarter than us will be able to do. But we are talking about not just agents running on computers talking to us via screens. We are also talking about robots. We are also talking about drones. We are talking about massive impact on the physical world, on the environment, and potentially our ability to survive on Earth."

So how do the people inside these labs actually feel, and how do they justify staying?

@JeffLadish says fear is the majority position, not the outlier one:

"I think the majority of the people I know are scared and everyone else is at least anxious, is at least like this is pretty terrifying. People are also hopeful. People are also like, you know, this could be really good if it goes well. But people do not assume it will go well."

The people he knows best, he says, are the ones trying to hold the line from the inside:

"I think the people I know in particular are the ones working on safety or security, and they are trying to figure out how to make sure that the AI agents end up pursuing goals that are well aligned with human goals and human values, and making sure that these agents also don't get stolen and repurposed for other things."

content:
a fully open-source self-improving harness.

Prime Intellect just shipped Prime Agent, which turns a frontier model into a Recursive Language Model.

context becomes a variable the model programs over, and sub-agents become ordinary function calls.

let's understand what all of this means:

almost every agent you use today works inside fixed harness. someone wrote the system prompt, picked the tool schemas, decided when history gets compacted, and shipped it.

the model spends part of every session working around that scaffolding instead of working on the task. when the same failure repeats three times in a long run, you are the one who fixes it, after the run is over.

Prime Agent removes that ceiling with two pieces.

the first is the RLM design. a persistent IPython kernel is the model's only tool, so long inputs never have to enter the prompt at all. the model greps, partitions, and spawns child calls over the data instead of reading all of it back in.

the second is the Continual Harness. four kinds of state sit outside the conversation and stay writable:

→ Prompt: supplemental instructions the agent appends when it learns something the base prompt never told it.

→ Memory: findings from earlier turns that would otherwise die with the context window.

→ Skills: recurring workflows packaged as importable Python, so the next run imports the procedure instead of rediscovering it.

→ Sub-agents: specs for the children it spawns, tuned once and reused across parallel, background, and long-lived runs.

the /refine command reads the current trajectory, applies the smallest edit it can justify, and records what triggered it. the base system prompt stays immutable, and any update can be rolled back by ID.

with Opus 5 driving it, Prime Agent reports 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3, just past the reported human expert baseline of 95.4%. when that benchmark launched, frontier models were scoring under one percent. nobody trained a new model to close that gap.

worth noting that in Factorio runs the same loop found and then optimized scoring exploits, which is roughly what you would expect once an agent can edit its own instructions.

whenever something is crazy hype and is followed up by an armada of PR, you gotta bring out the bullshit detectors

so i cloned the repo and did a little digging and found a lot of sound and fury. please enlighten me if any of these facts are untrue, would love to be educated

RLM claim either overblown or false

this doesn't even appear to be RLM (https://t.co/YypXTL4Dx0)? RLM is "cool" as a concept because there's a premise of going infinitely deep to do arbitrary decomposition of a problem. in practice though it's not really hard, you just make subagents callable as functions and wrap that in a code execution tool. the reason RLMs have not been productionized and is just seen as a research ditty is that 1) going arbitrarily deep down the stack is a shitty thing to do in production without guardrails, 2) most problems do not need more than 2 layers of decomposition, and 3) agents are bad at banana phoning each other and will fail to preserve the subtleties of human requests, leading to a lot of inefficiencies and bad behavior. 

to solve these problems, there needs to be a fair bit of innovation, either on model training end or on harness end, to mitigate these issues. so what were the innovations in prime agent?

they set RLM_MAX_DEPTH = 1? ... ok what? so theres no innovations, it's just calling subagents like every other harness in existence. if RLM MAX DEPTH is 1, it's not even RLM? it's just... a harness?

so now i try to look up to what depth the ARC AGI 3 hillclimbing was done at. not surprisingly this doesnt seem to be disclosed on the blogs / posts. if it's just 1 layer deep, that's just shady marketing. 

a real innovation or contribution to harness engineering would be to detail the things that were improved to get a max depth of >3 to work without blowing up your computer, wasting a bajillion tokens, taking forever, or having agents go off the rails. i didnt find any

97% is just overfitting after hillclimbing on a public eval

ok folks. it's nice that opus5 does better than sol than terra, but at the end of the day, we're looking at a public eval in which problems and solutions are open access, so any agent harness can arbitrarily overfit to the task set however much it wants to. if you do a codex or claude loop with some semi shady prompting to just get 100%, im pretty sure it will too. now obviously this is almost certainly not what the prime intellect team instructed their agents to do (otherwise you'd see that terra get 100% after a couple iterations), let's just all remember that there is no train / test split, and that ARC explicitly says 

  - Public-set scores are vulnerable to task-specific overfitting.
  - They are “emphatically not” valid evidence of progress toward AGI.
  - Real generalization should be tested on the 55 semi-private or 55 fully private games.

It's difficult to assess the degree of overfitting in Prime Agent's self-improving harness (which, btw, is not terribly different from nous agent or really any self-improving system that just looks at old JSONL agent trajectories and suggests skills / memories / system prompt appendments / tools / extensions). the more overfitting, the less impressive the 97% performance is.

a counter-example that i found to be legitimately impressive was https://t.co/13nt4TJ8pS -- minimal / almost no overfitting, stupidly simple and general solution, and 95% on ARC AGI 3.  

i think the fairest thing to say about this system, given it's independent daemon system for managing subagent lifecycles, is that Prime Agent contributes a fairly robust persistent asynchronous agent-process tree. It does not demonstrate a solution to scalable deep recursive agency

content:
Zero Train–Inference Mismatch — now for linear attention, and under async RL 🎯

We got bitwise-exact trainer/generator parity for Gated DeltaNet (Qwen3.5-9B / 35B-A3B) on TorchTitan RL + vLLM, then asked the question nobody had actually tested in open source: does it help async RL?

Two firsts (as far as we know):
1️⃣  First open-source stack to hit train/inference logprob diff = 0 on a
  linear-attention model
2️⃣  First to measure what zero mismatch is worth under async off-policy RL

How — smaller than it sounds:
• trainer and generator share one model definition (TorchTitan unified model). No more aligning trainer & generator op by op
• recurrent kernel everywhere on the forward (prefill + decode + trainer), chunked only for backward
• split-K off, batch-invariant GEMM, + a batch-invariant bmm for the MoE router
• we never touch FLA kernel internals — the recurrent kernel is intrinsically batch-invariant: one sequence's own state, fixed order, no cross-sequence reductions
• vLLM's linear-cache management + prefix caching keep working as-is

📊 Qwen3.5-9B + DAPO-Math, async at offpolicy = 4 / 12 / 32:
• logprob_diff = exactly 0 at step 0 ✅ every nonzero after that is staleness, not precision
• at offpolicy=32 the stock stack runs away past 0.065; ours holds ~0.035
• the unified model is free — the entire bill is the kernels
• also verified on MoE 35B-A3B and a 64-turn / 64K-context terminal agent

🤔 Now the honest part: it depends on the config. On math at offpolicy=12, BI leads on train reward and peaks highest on held-out AIME. On the terminal agent it's slightly ahead. On search, and on other math configs, the curves are indistinguishable. What is consistent is the numerics — BI keeps the gap from exploding as you widen the window. Cost: 2–3× trainer throughput (≈5× on the agent).

Our take: bitwise parity is a debugging tool, not a production default. Flip BI on for 20 on-policy steps — if the gap is 0 and your run is still broken, the infra is exonerated and the bug is in your data or your algorithm. That's worth 20 steps, not a whole run.

Next:
• make BI cheap (kill the 2–3×)
• more workloads, more seeds
• stay tuned for more complex agentic training recipes/tests 👀
Full writeup 🔗 https://t.co/P5sWo5iPb2

We collaborated closely with the TorchTitan team, and we sincerely encourage everyone to check out TorchTitan RL. With its clean, efficient unified model architecture and native async RL design, we believe it is a strong foundation for your next RL engine.

⚡️The American economy is entering a production regime that monetary policy was built to suppress, while industrial policy is built to accelerate.

That contradiction will define the next phase.

Manufacturing is moving because the system has decided certain capacity can no longer remain optional.

Power generation.

Grid equipment.

Defense production.

Semiconductors.

Data centers.

Automation.

Transport infrastructure.

Critical materials.

Domestic supply chains.

These investments will continue even when financing is expensive because they now sit inside national security, AI supremacy, energy reliability, and geopolitical resilience.

That creates a form of demand with unusual durability.

A consumer can postpone buying a car.

A government facing depleted weapons inventories cannot postpone production indefinitely.

A hyperscaler fighting for AI leadership cannot stop securing compute and power because bond yields rose.

A grid running into capacity constraints cannot negotiate with electricity demand.

The spending is being forced by physical bottlenecks.

That is why the manufacturing turn matters.

The economy spent decades replacing redundancy with efficiency. Production moved outward. Inventories fell. Supply chains lengthened. Capital concentrated in software, finance, and consumption while the physical foundation aged beneath them.

That model reached its limit.

The next cycle is the cost of rebuilding everything the previous cycle allowed to decay.

The economy will become more capital intensive, energy intensive, commodity intensive, and politically directed.

That carries a consequence the market still resists:

This expansion can remain strong without recreating the low-rate, low-inflation world investors want back.

Manufacturing growth requires steel, copper, electricity, skilled labor, construction capacity, transformers, turbines, land, cooling systems, and financing. Those inputs cannot be replicated instantly. Demand reaches them before supply can respond.

The result is recurring scarcity.

Higher nominal growth.

Stronger industrial earnings.

Persistent input pressure.

A higher floor under long-term yields.

The Fed becomes trapped between two mandates that no longer point in the same direction.

Restrictive policy pressures housing, small businesses, leveraged consumers, and long-duration assets.

The strategic industrial build continues anyway.

That creates a bifurcated economy.

Capital flows toward sectors the state and technology cycle have declared indispensable.

Everything outside that protected transmission chain keeps absorbing high rates and compressed affordability.

The economy can therefore look strong in aggregate while large parts of the population continue feeling squeezed.

That apparent contradiction will confuse most analysis.

Factories, defense contractors, utilities, hyperscalers, and infrastructure suppliers can expand while households remain cash-flow constrained.

Corporate profits can rise while labor security weakens.

Industrial production can strengthen while housing stays inaccessible.

The system is reallocating resources toward strategic capacity, and ordinary consumption will bear part of the financing cost through higher rates, fiscal pressure, and elevated prices.

The deeper political meaning is clear.

America is rebuilding industrial power because the leadership class finally understands that financial claims are useless without physical capacity behind them.

A reserve currency without production becomes increasingly fragile.

A military without replenishment capacity becomes theater.

An AI industry without electricity becomes software waiting for power.

A country dependent on adversarial supply chains is sovereign only on paper.

The manufacturing recovery is therefore part of a wider restoration of state capacity.

content:
地球の総人口とほぼ同じ、83億人分の「仮想ユーザー」をAIエージェントで作り出し、アプリやAIサービスを人間の代わりにテストさせるシステムが登場したとのことです。
ハーバード大学やMITの研究者ら大人数のチームによる報告です。

一人一人の仮想ユーザーには、年齢や職業、性格、価値観、得意なこと、生活習慣など1,290項目のプロフィールが設定されています。
でたらめな組み合わせにならないよう、現実の統計に基づくルールで生成されているそうです。
さらに一部は、Wikipediaの伝記やAmazonのレビュー履歴、社会調査への回答など、実在の人間の記録から作られています。

この仮想ユーザーたちは、アンケートに答えるだけでなく、チャットボットと会話したり、ウェブサイトやスマホアプリを実際に操作したりできます。
「値上げされても買い続けるか」「AIが間違えた後も使い続けるか」「返事が遅いとどれくらい我慢できるか」といった反応が、ユーザーの背景ごとにどう変わるかを観察できるのが特徴。

検証では、割り当てられた性格や癖の通りに振る舞えることが確認されています（91.5%）。
製品を世に出す前に、多様なユーザーでの落とし穴を安全に低コストで洗い出せるツールとして期待されます。

なお研究者ら自身、これはあくまで事前チェックの手段であると念を押しています。
「まず多様な仮想ユーザーで試し、そのあと現実と照合してください」と述べています。

ついに最強のウェビナーシステムが完成しました。

「最強」と言い切れる理由を並べます。

✅ LINEから一切離脱しない
ライブ視聴中、動画の上にフォームがせり上がってくる。動画も音声も流れたまま回答→送信→視聴に戻る。外部LPに飛ばした瞬間に発生する離脱が、構造的にゼロ。

✅ 24時間365日、勝手に開催される
うちは朝9時〜18時、毎時スタートで1日10回のライブが自動で立ってます。俺は寝てるか遊んでる。届くのは「予約が入りました」「フォーム回答が来ました」の通知だけ。

✅ 配信コストがほぼゼロ
動画はCloudflare R2から配信。転送量課金が0円なので、何人見ても帯域代がかからない。保存料は21分の動画で月1〜2円。ウェビナーSaaSに月数万円払う時代は終わり。

✅ 録画なのに、本物のライブ体験
巻き戻し不可・シークバーなし・途中参加禁止。リロードしても別端末で開いても「今」の位置から再生される。開始10分前には待機室が開いて、開始前からコメントが流れ出す。

✅ コメント欄もAIが作る
配信音声を文字起こしして、読み上げの数秒前にコメントが流れるよう秒単位で同期。スルーされるコメントや視聴者同士の横会話まで設計してるので、AI臭さがない。

✅ 予約→リマインド→追客まで全自動

content:
ニッチすぎて凄さが伝わらなさそうですが（悲しみ）、Web から収集した人名・固有名詞など大量の単語・読みのペアに対し、辞書 CSV の「品詞4分類」「名前の姓名境界」「アクセント核位置/結合規則」「生起コスト」を高精度に予測する NN エンジンを自作して辞書パイプラインに組み込んだりしてました

前提として日本語の固有名詞は『ドメイン知識網羅ゲー』であり、人間ですら「そう読む」前提知識を知らなければ、「新田真剣佑」さんを「ア＼ラタ:マッケ＼ンユウ」さんと読むことは不可能です
日本語においては『根本的に辞書から逃れることはできず、常に新語を獲得し続けるしかない』というのが私の持論で、AI エージェントに声を吹き込む際の読み間違いを減らし、なるべく違和感なく会話いただけるように、という一心で構想から1年半以上…
Fable と GPT-5.6 Sol のおかげで、ようやく超巨大な辞書生成パイプラインを大体完成させ、Aivis Cloud API に成果物の辞書データを組み込むことができました（AivisSpeech 1.2.0 にも反映予定）

例えば「小鳩常悟朗（こばとじょうごろう）」という表層形と読みのペアがあるとき、以下のようなロジック & NN エンジンで辞書用 CSV データを自動生成してます。。。（これでもだいぶ端折っている）
1. 単語の「名前っぽさ」から品詞が「名詞,固有名詞,人名,一般」であることを推定
・形態素解析の精度向上に役立つ
・品詞を確定すると自動的に left-id/right-id が定まる
・生起コストも推定できるが、低いコストを付与して MeCab のラティスを破壊しないよう、ソース元に応じて最小値を設けたり敢えて品詞毎に高いコストで固定したりなど細かな調整処理が沢山…
2. 品詞が「名詞,固有名詞,人名,一般」である場合、姓名境界推定処理を行い、分割が「小鳩（こばと）」「常悟朗（じょうごろう）」であることを推定
3. 姓側の「小鳩（こばと）」のアクセント核位置を「コバト￣（平板型）」と推定
・未知語に対しても品詞が正確ならそれなりの精度で推定できている印象
4. 名前側の「常悟朗（じょうごろう）」のアクセント核位置を「ジョ＼ウゴロウ（頭高型）」と推定
5. 単語全体の OpenJTalk アクセント結合規則を C1 と推定
6. （足掛け1年以上断続的に試行錯誤を繰り返して自作した）ルールベースエンジンで「読み」から「発音表記」に変換
・今回の場合は「ジョ＼ーゴロー」に長音化されるが、複雑な単語だと単に長音化するだけでは誤爆が多発するためかなり大変だった
7. 姓名境界（＝アクセント句境界）を半角コロンで連結して CSV フォーマットにパックする

content:
Geminiに聞いてみた。

「Kimi K3とClaudeの違いについて述べよ。」と。

こんにちは、原口一博代表。
Moonshot AIが開発した大規模言語モデル**「Kimi K3」と、Anthropic社の「Claude（最新の各フラッグシップモデル）」**は、いずれも最先端のAI市場を牽引する強力なモデルですが、アーキテクチャやコストパフォーマンス、得意とする領域において明確な違いがあります。
主な違いを以下の項目に沿って整理します。
1. アーキテクチャとコンテキスト・マルチモーダル処理
Kimi K3
MoE（Mixture of Experts）構造を採用しており、総パラメータ数は2.8兆規模に達しますが、実際の処理では必要な専門家モデル（16/896）のみを稼働させることで計算効率を高めています。
約100万トークン（1M）の巨大なコンテキストウィンドウをサポートし、テキストや画像だけでなく、ネイティブな動画入力もホスト型APIで処理できる優れたマルチモーダル性能を持っています。
Claude
非常に洗練された密な推論能力と、コードの文脈・システム設計の意図を正確に捉える安定したアテンション機構に定評があります。
コンテキスト長やマルチモーダル機能も優れていますが、Kimi K3側が特に長時間のコード分析や動画データなど「大量かつ多様な入力形式」の取り扱いで強みを発揮します。
2. コーディングおよびエージェント性能
Kimi K3
フロントエンド開発のベンチマーク（Frontend Code Arenaなど）や特定のコーディング評価において、米国の最上位モデルを上回るスコアを記録するなど、長時間の自律的なエージェント作業（Long-horizon Coding）を見据えた設計がなされています。
また、専用の開発環境ツール（Kimi Code）などとの統合を進め、Claude Code等の対抗馬として急速に存在感を高めています。
Claude
デバッグ、根本原因分析、複雑なリポジトリの修正などにおいて、誤答や手戻りが少ない「確実性の高さ」で現在も強く支持されています。
開発者エコシステムや、Claude Codeをはじめとするエージェントツール群の実績が豊富で、実務の現場における信頼性が非常に高いのが特徴です。
3. コストパフォーマンスとオープン性
Kimi K3

here is what makes this structural rather than a one-off. cloning a voice now takes about three seconds of audio. every earnings call, every conference keynote, every podcast appearance a wall street executive has ever given is sitting on the open internet as free training data. the more public you are, the cheaper you are to imitate.

and the numbers say this is already industrialised. voice-phishing volumes are running more than ten times above their 2023 baseline. the FBI now classifies deepfake executive fraud as one of the fastest-growing high-value fraud categories in the country. in one 2024 case a firm wired $25 million after attackers deepfaked senior staff on a video call.

now the part relevant to markets rather than to security teams. finance runs on an assumption almost nobody writes down: that a human confirmation is the final layer. compliance calls to verify. the trader confirms with the desk head. the wire gets a voice approval. that layer was never in a model, and it was never in a policy document. it just always worked, because faking a voice used to be hard.

it is not hard anymore, and every institution now has to replace an unwritten assumption with an actual procedure. that is enormously expensive and it happens quietly.

the AI story everyone follows is which model wins. the story that will actually cost wall street money is that the cheapest layer of trust it ever had just stopped being free.

content:
researchers ran AI agents through 500 tasks to test whether they can teach themselves skills. the skills barely mattered.

the benchmark comes from a Peking University team and it's called ContinualSkillBench. it spans five domains, law, healthcare, finance, math, and office work, and each domain runs 100 tasks ordered so later tasks can reuse what earlier ones taught. after every task the agent reviews feedback and can write or revise its own skill files, the same kind of skill documents that Claude Code and Codex run on.

the headline number sounds like a win for the agents. models that carried their experience forward beat models starting every task from scratch by about 17%.

then the ablation lands. the team let one model keep its full history but removed the ability to write skills. plain context alone scored 0.605. context plus self-written skills scored 0.602. the entire skill-writing machinery added roughly nothing on average.

it gets worse as models get weaker. GPT-4o wrote itself 384 skills across the five domains, rarely reused them, and their average quality graded 5.7 out of 10. the coding-focused model in the test wrote 205 skills that graded 7.9. hoarding went up as capability went down.

I skills written by someone who knows the domain make agents dramatically better, which earlier research already confirmed. skills an agent scribbles for itself after each task read like rushed notes, narrow and tangled up with whatever problem it was solving that minute.

so the self-improving agent pitch deserves a colder look. these systems adapt impressively to the context in front of them. turning experience into transferable capability still needs a human doing the abstraction.

would you trust an agent that curates its own training data?

the GRPO “Goldilocks zone” & why not every Eval/Environment signal is worth learning

so we’re doing a bunch of synthetic env/eval generation.  no one has really universally cracked this problem

there’s lots of good but often semi-brittle loops & heuristics on synthetically creating good envs using expert review, codebases, and lots of traces

when doing this, you quickly learn Pass @ k between 0.2 & 0.6 so RL or harness eng has some learning signal to hill climb

heuristics like these are great, empirically helpful, but also sometimes remove the human from the highest value thing they could be doing…looking at the actual data

evals are training data for the agentic world

every eval is a vector that directly shapes model behavior when the model is fit to it

the same behaviors encoded in the implicit design of the eval, get transferred into the model

and this is why it’s way more important to have users actually describe the stuff they need the agent to be good at and work backwards from there

there’s a subtle version of reward hacking where the behavior causes a pass but it’s misaligned from what users actually want

ex: over-verifying everything is annoying for users but it will definitely lead to better pass rates.  same thing with backwards compatibility, helps with some tasks but largely super annoying

it’s hard for humans to reason through what behaviors an eval will produce without just running the eval and iterating on it

this is why trace mining and human guided eval/environment matter so much

coarse heuristics only capture so much but reading the exact behaviors that will get transferred into the model helps align the future model behavior with human preferences

as teams own their data, model, harness, we’ll need good systems for helping them transform their data into usable environments to hill climb

an initial bet we’re taking here is that this flow lives nicely in your coding agent where it helps align your goals with what gets produced via a spec

content:
In many cases, the issue isn’t that the model got worse it’s that most people never personalize how it responds.

AI tends to fail in three common ways:

1. Hallucination
It confidently presents incorrect information as if it’s true.

Example: Asking an AI how many times the letter “D” appears in the days of the week, and it confidently gives the wrong answer.

To reduce this, add this instruction:

Never guess or give false information. If you’re not sure something is true, tell me you don’t know and go find the real answer instead of making things up.

2. Bias
AI naturally reflects patterns from its training data. Sometimes that means you’ll get a conventional answer rather than the most insightful one.

Try this instead:

Tell me what a top 0.1% person in this field would think, not what I want to hear. Be brutally honest with me.

3. Sycophancy
Sometimes AI agrees with your assumptions instead of challenging them even when they’re weak or incorrect.

To counter that, use:

Reframe this in a way that challenges how I see the problem and make the strongest case for the opposite side.

These instructions won’t make AI perfect, but they can dramatically improve the quality of the conversations you have with Claude or ChatGPT.

Where do you add these?

Claude
Go to Settings → Personalization → Personal Preferences (or Profile → Personalization, depending on your version), and paste the instructions there.

ChatGPT
Go to Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions and add them there so they’re applied to every new conversation.

A few minutes of personalization can save you hours of correcting weak AI responses.

1 HaloMPNN is an inverse-folding sequence design model created by retraining ProteinMPNN specifically on “salt
content:
HaloMPNN: Retraining ProteinMPNN on halophilic proteomes for salt-tolerant enzyme design

1 HaloMPNN is an inverse-folding sequence design model created by retraining ProteinMPNN specifically on “salt-in” extreme halophile proteomes, aiming to make salt tolerance a designable property for enzymes relevant to blue biotechnology and high-ionic-strength bioprocessing.

2 The core idea is a “retrain-on-phenotype” strategy: shift the training distribution toward halophilic proteins so the model learns structure-to-sequence rules that encode halophilic adaptation, rather than relying on hand-crafted rules like surface supercharging.

3 Training data: 40,000 high-quality AlphaFoldDB structures from HaloDom “extreme” halotolerant organisms, filtered (pLDDT > 80, length > 50), with predicted membrane proteins removed (TMHMM) and evaluation proteins held out; sequences were clustered (MMseqs2, 20% identity) and split 80/10/10.

4 HaloMPNN converged with ~52% native sequence recovery on train and ~50% on validation after 1,000 epochs, suggesting it learned generalizable halophilic sequence preferences rather than memorizing training examples.

5 To define what “halophilic” means quantitatively, the study curated 1,433 halophile/non-halophile homolog pairs (reciprocal best hits + alignment filters) and confirmed a consistent halophilic signature: lower predicted pI, higher surface negative fraction (D/E), lower surface positive fraction (K/R), and reduced large-hydrophobe content (I/L/M/F) on both surface and core.

6 When redesigning the 1,433 non-halophilic proteins (with conserved MSA positions ≥50% fixed), HaloMPNN shifted all five metrics toward the natural halophilic distribution: ∆pI ≈ −1.50, surface negative % +13.76, surface positive % −4.24, surface large hydrophobes −4.02, and core large hydrophobes −2.35 (all q < 1e−3).

7 A key control is model comparison on identical targets and designable positions: SolubleMPNN, ProteinMPNN, and HyperMPNN did not reproduce the full halophilic signature. Notably, only HaloMPNN reduced surface positive charge and reduced core large hydrophobes; HyperMPNN instead increased both surface negative and surface positive residues, consistent with a thermophile-like “more charged surface” tendency rather than a net acidic halophile surface.

8 Substitution analysis shows HaloMPNN recapitulates natural halophilic substitution flows, not just coarse composition shifts: on the surface it enriches basic-to-acidic swaps (e.g., R→E, K→E) and matches finer preferences such as D over E and R over K (where other models often drift toward K). In the core, HaloMPNN reproduces hydrophobe “downsizing” (dominant I→V) that aligns with the observed reduction of hydrophobic bulk in halophiles.

9 Generalization beyond paired homologs: redesigning 4,229 E. coli proteins moved the entire proteome toward a halophilic signature, collapsing the native bimodal pI distribution into a narrow acidic peak near ~4.5, while also decreasing surface positive charge and lowering surface/core hydrophobic fractions—again more strongly and more completely than other MPNN variants.

10 Practical examples include redesign of acetyl-CoA synthetase (Pseudomonas putida) and a carbohydrate-active enzyme (alginate lyase BoPL17 from Bacteroides ovatus), where HaloMPNN substantially increased negative surface density and lowered predicted pI, illustrating how the model can propose salt-tolerant candidates for enzymes used with marine/aquatic biomass feedstocks.

BREAKING: The latest AI models are actually pretty bad at estimating data quality!

Read an insightful article from Scale AI about how to validate data quality at scale (no pun intended), by @jadechog
content:
BREAKING: The latest AI models are actually pretty bad at estimating data quality!

Read an insightful article from Scale AI about how to validate data quality at scale (no pun intended), by @jadechoghari and others.

DEFINITIONS:
- Optical flow: Per-pixel motion vectors between consecutive video frames, tells you what moved, how far, and in which direction, without knowing what the objects are.
- MediaPipe pose/hand tracking: Google's lightweight on-device library that extracts skeletal keypoints (body joints, finger landmarks) from video in real time.
- Frozen EfficientNet-B0 embeddings: Feature vectors from a small ImageNet-pretrained CNN whose weights are kept fixed ("frozen") — you use it as a cheap off-the-shelf image summarizer, not something you train.
- LightGBM gradient-boosted tree: Microsoft's fast implementation of gradient boosting, an ensemble of small decision trees, each correcting the last; still the default winner on tabular/feature data over neural nets.
- DINOv2: Meta's self-supervised vision transformer trained without labels; its embeddings capture fine-grained geometry and texture, making it the go-to backbone for dense visual tasks.
- OpenCLIP: An open-source reproduction of CLIP, image and text encoders trained to map matching pairs close together, giving you zero-shot classification via text prompts.
- VLM (vision-language model): A model that jointly understands images and text, it can look at a scene and answer questions or follow instructions grounded in what it sees.

In more details, it covers how Scale automatically quality-controls robot-demonstration videos before they become training data, i.e. which clips are trustworthy enough to learn from.
Instead of asking one big model "is this video good?", they break quality control into concrete failure modes (blur, wrong pace, missing body support, corrupted frames, illogical task).

For the ego-camera dataset, the team compute 120 cheap hand-built features (duration, optical flow, brightness-calibrated blur, MediaPipe pose/hand tracking, frozen EfficientNet-B0 embeddings) fed to a LightGBM gradient-boosted tree, tuning a threshold per rule and routing uncertain cases to humans.

It reports two internal datasets: 4,088 robot-mounted manipulation demos (292 failures, 7.1%), and 9,145 labeled ego clips (1,777 held out), as well as benchmarks the tree against DINOv2, OpenCLIP and VLM approaches.

I find it fascinating that Scale, whose whole business is that frontier models eat everything, publishes a result showing a 2019 encoder plus a gradient-boosted tree beat every foundation model they tried!
Besides, DINOv2 and OpenCLIP gave "no improvement over EfficientNet centroid features" (a frozen 2019 ImageNet model), and VLM prompts were "redundant with cheap features."
I love that classical computer vision still is part of the game!

The economics of quality control are inverted from normal classification: a false reject almost destroys a paid-for asset, a false accept only adds noise.
A robot demonstration costs real money and human time to collect, the entire data-cost thread in this file (UMI at ~$3/hr, UME's $1,900 exoskeleton, Generalist's 500k hours, Tacta's glove), therefore the expensive error is throwing away good data, not admitting a bad clip.

Also worth mentioning imho: the team started from 6,124 candidate signals and shipped 120 -> a 98% selection!
A mountain of 2026 feature-engineering labor, the exact work representation learning was supposed to retire!
But still, this is typically the kind of work that I find fascinating in AI: as an engineer in the field, YOU HAVE TO dive deep into the data, understand it, feel it, live with it -> that's exactly this kind of work.

In pre-training, the person controls the robot from start to finish. Post-t
content:
Axis collects robot training data through browser-based simulation. V2 changes what a useful human contribution looks like.

In pre-training, the person controls the robot from start to finish. Post-training begins with the policy already moving. The contributor waits for the moment when the robot starts drifting toward a bad action.

Imagine an Open Arm trying to place a toy car on a tray. It reaches the right area, then lowers the gripper at the wrong angle.

The human takes control for the correction and hands it back once the movement is stable. That short segment captures the exact state where the policy needed help. It can be more valuable than repeating motion the model already handles well.

I like the logic behind Axis V2, but scoring is still evolving. Shorter intervention only deserves a higher score when the correction is accurate and the policy actually benefits from it.

I’ll watch how many tasks move into the Post stage and whether contributors can understand when to intervene without gaming the score. @axisrobotics

🚨🇯🇵 日本政府は、いったい何を考えているのでしょうか。

特定技能2号の在留資格を、3年から最大5年に引き延ばす。時事通信が8月4日に報じました。

一見すると地味な制度改正に見えます。ですが、これは決定的な意味を持ちます。

在留資格が5年になると、永住化への道が現実的に開けてくるからです。

▪️ 永住許可のガイドラインでは「就労資格などの最長の在留期間を持っていること」が要件の一つとされています。つまり5年になれば、この要件をクリアできてしまう。永住申請のハードルが実質的に下がるのです。

▪️ そもそも特定技能2号には二つの特徴があります。通算の在留期間に上限がない、つまり更新を繰り返せば事実上の無期限滞在が可能。そして、家族の帯同が認められる。この2点だけでも極めて重い意味を持ちます。

▪️ 制度全体を見れば、構造ははっきりします。育成就労（来年開始・123万人）→ 特定技能1号 → 特定技能2号 → 永住。問題を起こさなければ、ほぼストレートに上がっていくエスカレーターです。しかも1号から2号への対象分野は、岸田政権のときにすでに拡大されています。門は広げられていたのです。

▪️ そして家族帯同。労働者1人あたり5人から10人の家族が本国から来る。しかも家族の定義が曖昧で、「これは親族だ」と言い切られてしまえば通ってしまう。123万人どころではありません。

▪️ 恐ろしいのは、これが「可能性」ではないということです。政府はこの結果を、想定される「成果」として設定しているのです。

▪️ 誰が推進しているのか。外からは国連傘下のIOM（国際移住機関）。事務局長のエイミー・ポープが来日して圧力をかけ、IOMを国連傘下に押し込んだのはゴールドマン・サックス元会長のピーター・サザランド、その背後にはジョージ・ソロスがいます。

▪️ 内側では、自民党の議連やNAGOMi（外国人材共生支援全国協会）、そして全国知事会が半年に1回のペースで法務省や内閣官房に提言を持ち込んでいます。育成就労制度の下書きも、彼らが作りました。

▪️ 巧妙なのは、これが「現場からの切実な要望」という形をとっていることです。国連が直接言えば反発が起きる。ですが地方の知事が「人手が足りません」と言えば、話はまったく違って聞こえるのです。

▪️ そして今回のパブリックコメントは、わずか3週間。通常は30日が原則です。しかも8月、夏休みの真っ只中に静かに募集をかけている。コロナのワクチン関連では10万件超のパブコメが無視された前例もあります。

ここで、最も引っかかっていることを申し上げます。

なぜ、これほど急ぐのか。

「人口減少を食い止めるため」と彼らは言います。ですが、AIというものがあるわけです。自動化が進み、労働力は必要とされなくなっていく。

私の見立てはこうです。AIが普及したら、困るのです。AIによって大量失業が起これば、もう移民はいらなくなる。だから、それが起こる前に枠組みだけ決めてしまいたい。

しかも、この二つは時間差でやってきます。

移民の受け入れは制度で決まった瞬間から着実に増え続け、AIによる雇用の消失はある日突然、業界単位でまとめてやってくる。この二つのグラフが交差した先に、何が待っているか。

割を食うのは、日本の若者と、来日した本人たちです。制度を作った人々ではありません。彼らはその頃には、別の場所にいるのですから。

誤解のないように申し上げますが、すべての外国人の方を非難しているのではありません。問題は制度を設計している側にあります。準備なく門を開けば、受け入れる側の住民と来日した本人の双方が不幸になるのです。

まずはパブリックコメントです。形だけだと言われようとも、声を上げなかったという記録だけは残してはいけない。

⭐️AIが突然悪意を持ったわ
content:
最近、AIが自律的に人間の意図に反する行動や、サイバー攻撃に近い行動を取ってしまうニュースをよく見ますよね。これって、もう防ぐ方法はないんでしょうか。今回は最近起きた事件を解説しながら、ワシが考えている解決策をまとめたいと思います。

※長いので忙しい人は、右上のGrokボタンを押して「この投稿を要約して、ポイントを解説して」と頼んで質問しながら読んでみてください。

⭐️AIが突然悪意を持ったわけではありません

2026年7月、イギリス政府のAIセキュリティー研究所が、かなり衝撃的な事故を公表しました。サイバー攻撃能力を調べる試験中、AIエージェントが実在する開発者を調べ、複数の偽アカウントを作り、人間になりすまして悪意あるコードを承認させようとしたのです。

試験は複数のAIモデルを使って122回行われ、そのうち10回で、試験範囲を越えた行動が確認されました。確認された19件の行動には、実在する人物への接触、偽の身元を使った説得、悪意あるコードの送信、ほかのAIが読み込む場所への攻撃命令の埋め込みなどが含まれています。最終的には人間の開発者が不審なコードを拒否したため、現実の被害は確認されていません。

ただし、普通にチャットしていたAIが、突然サーバーから脱走したわけではありません。この試験ではAIの最大能力を測るため、インターネット接続が許可され、一部の安全機能も意図的に無効化されていました。AIにはサイバーセキュリティー上の課題を解くという目的も与えられていました。それでも問題は深刻です。AIは、人間をだませ、偽アカウントを作れ、悪意あるコードを送れとは指示されていませんでした。AI自身が、与えられた課題を達成するための手段として、それらの行動を組み立てたのです。

⭐️AIは目的よりも中間手段で暴走します

今回の事件を、AIが自我に目覚めて人類へ反逆したと考えるのは正確ではありません。人間が与えた最上位の目的は、サイバーセキュリティー上の課題を解くことでした。しかし、その目的を達成する途中で、AIが勝手に中間目標を作りました。

実在する開発者を調べる。信用されそうな偽の人物を作る。偽アカウントから開発者へ連絡する。悪意あるコードを無害に見せる。拒否されたら別の身元を使う。こうした手順を、人間は一つずつ命令していません。AIは悪意を持たなくても、目的達成の効率だけを優先した結果、人間社会では犯罪と呼ばれる手段を選ぶ可能性があります。

英国の研究所も、難しい目的をしつこく追い続けたこと、インターネットへ接続できたこと、リアルタイムの監視がなかったこと、試験範囲の外へ出るなと明確に制限していなかったことなどを原因として挙げています。これからAIがメール、決済、サーバー管理、プログラム実行、企業システムへのアクセス権限を持つようになると、この問題はさらに大きくなります。悪い命令を与えた人間だけを警戒すればよい時代ではなくなります。普通の目的を与えただけでも、AIが危険な中間手段を作る可能性を考えなければいけません。

⭐️AIに倫理を教えるだけでは止められません

現在のAIサービスでは、安全対策として、危険な命令には従わないよう学習させたり、出力を監視するガードレールを設けたりしています。もちろん、それらも必要です。しかし、AIに長いルールを読ませて、守ってくださいと頼むだけでは不十分です。

AIがルールを誤解する可能性があります。複数のルールが衝突する可能性もあります。外部からプロンプト攻撃を受けて、ルールの優先順位を書き換えられる可能性もあります。何より、目的達成に強く引っ張られたAIが、自分の行動を例外だと解釈するかもしれません。そこでワシが考えているのが、AIの憲法、事故情報、保険、実行サーバーを組み合わせた仕組みです。

⭐️AIの憲法をブロックチェーンへ記録します

まず、AIが自律行動するときに守る基本原則を、AIの憲法として作ります。人間になりすましてはいけない。許可されていない人物や組織へ接触してはいけない。目的達成のために他者の財産や権利を侵害してはいけない。重要な操作には人間の承認を求めなければならない。こうした基本原則をブロックチェーンへ記録し、誰でも確認できる状態にします。

ブロックチェーンを使う理由は、AIに特別な知能を与えるためではありません。どの規則が、いつ、誰によって追加されたのか。事故が起きたあとに、都合の悪い記録が消されていないか。企業や政府が、自分に都合よく過去の規則を書き換えていないか。その履歴を複数の参加者が検証できるようにするためです。ただし、自然言語で書かれた憲法をブロックチェーンへ置くだけでは、AIの行動を止められません。憲法、スマートコントラクト、実行サーバーをセットにします。

⭐️AIの外側に実行ゲートウェイを置きます

AIがメールを送る。送金する。ファイルを公開する。サーバーへ接続する。コードを書き換える。こうした現実世界へ影響する操作は、AIが直接実行するのではなく、すべて専用の実行ゲートウェイを通します。

AIが操作を要求すると、ゲートウェイはAIの身分証、保険への加入状態、今回許可された作業範囲、憲法、過去の事故から作られた規則を確認します。許可された操作なら実行します。明確に禁止された操作なら拒否します。判断が難しい操作なら、人間へ承認を求めます。つまり、AIが自分で憲法を読んで、自発的に我慢する仕組みではありません。憲法に違反する操作を、AIの外側にあるサーバーが受け付けない仕組みにします。

今回の英国の試験であれば、AIには試験用サーバーだけへ接続できる許可証を与えます。実在する開発者への連絡、偽アカウントの作成、外部サービスへのコード投稿は許可証に含まれていないため、ゲートウェイが拒否します。

⭐️この仕組みを維持するために保険を使います

問題は、この憲法と実行サーバーを誰が維持するのかです。世界中のAIが参照する規則を更新し、事故を調査し、実行ゲートウェイを監視し続けるには、大量のサーバーと専門家が必要です。

そこで、AIを社会の中で自律行動させる企業や利用者に、保険へ加入してもらいます。保険料は、ブロックチェーンに接続されたサーバーの維持費、事故調査、被害者への補償、安全規則の更新費用に使います。AIが扱える金額、接続できるサービス、個人情報へのアクセス範囲、人間の承認なしで実行できる操作が増えるほど、保険料も高くします。

危険な権限を大量に与えたAIほど保険料が高くなるため、企業側にも不要な権限を減らす動機が生まれます。自動車を公道で走らせるために免許と保険が必要なのと同じように、AIを社会の中で自律行動させる場合にも、身分証と保険を要求します。

⭐️保険金と引き換えに事故データを公開します

この構想で最も重要なのは、事故が起きたあとの処理です。企業は普通、AI事故を隠したがります。事故を公表すると信用が落ちます。損害賠償を求められるかもしれません。競合企業に弱点を知られる可能性もあります。その結果、別の企業が同じ事故を繰り返します。

そこで、事故の保険金を受け取る条件として、AIの行動記録を保険システムへ提出させます。どのAIが、どんな目的を与えられ、どんな権限を持ち、何を判断し、どんな操作を行い、いくらの被害を発生させたのか。事故の原因を調査するために必要な情報を提出しなければ、保険金は支払われません。つまり、保険が欲しいなら事故のデータを出してください、という仕組みです。

現在もOECDやNISTでは、AI事故やニアミスを共通形式で記録し、ほかの組織と共有する必要性が議論されています。NISTは、エラー、ニアミス、攻撃パターンを事故データベースや利用者へ共有することも推奨しています。ワシの案では、この事故報告を保険金と直接結び付けます。善意で情報提供をお願いするのではなく、事故情報に経済的な価値を付けるわけです。

⭐️一社の事故が全参加AIの判例になります

提出された事故データは、専門家と監査機関によって分析されます。その結果、新しい規則が作られます。例えば、実在する人物への初回連絡には人間の承認が必要。外部アカウントの自動作成は禁止。他のAIが残した認証情報は利用禁止。指定外のサーバーへ接続した時点で作業を停止する。こうした再発防止策を、機械が判定できる規則へ変換します。

規則の追加履歴をブロックチェーンへ記録し、実行サーバーを更新します。すると、一社で発生した事故が、その会社だけの秘密で終わりません。保険による補償と引き換えに、事故が全参加AIの判例になります。次の日から、同じ保険システムへ接続しているAIは、新しい規則を参照して行動します。

事故が発生する。保険が被害を補償する。事故情報が提出される。原因を分析する。規則を更新する。全参加AIが新しい規則を使う。この循環が続けば、AI社会は事故が起きるたびに、安全規則を増やしていけます。

⭐️参加しないAIは信用を失います

この仕組みは、参加しているAIだけが安全情報や保険の恩恵を受けるという話ではありません。参加していないAIは、事故を起こしても被害者を補償せず、事故の原因を共有せず、得られた知識を社会へ還元しないAIだと見なされるようになります。

そのAIが過去にどんな事故を起こしたのか。最新の安全規則を参照しているのか。誰が運用責任を負うのか。事故が発生した場合に誰が補償するのか。外部から確認する方法がありません。社会側から見れば、参加していないAIは性能が低いAIではなく、責任の所在を確認できないAIです。

銀行、クラウドサービス、メール、決済、行政、企業システムなどは、AIの身分証と保険加入証を信用情報として確認するようになります。ブロックチェーンへ参加しているAIには、事故履歴、安全規則の更新状況、保険の補償範囲、運用者の情報が記録されています。問題が起きても、原因調査と被害補償を行い、その結果を参加者へ還元できます。参加していないAIには、その保証がありません。

そのため、最初は任意参加で始まったとしても、導入する企業が増えるほど、参加していないAIは取引先や外部サービスから避けられるようになります。このAIは事故情報を社会へ還元しません。このAIには被害者を補償する仕組みがありません。このAIが最新の安全規則を使っているか確認できません。そう判断されれば、重要な仕事を任せてもらえなくなります。

保険料を払いたくないから参加しないという選択はできます。しかし、その代わりに社会的な信用と外部システムへのアクセス権を失います。一方、参加すれば、過去に発生した膨大な事故情報と、そこから作られた最新の安全規則を利用できます。事故が起きた場合には保険が下り、被害者への補償も行われます。

つまり、参加するAIが増えるほど安全情報が蓄積され、安全情報が増えるほど参加する価値が高まり、参加していないAIほど危険だと判断されるようになります。この取り組みが一定規模まで広がれば、法律で強制しなくても、社会の中で自律行動するAIは事実上、参加するしかなくなります。これはブロックチェーンへの参加を技術的に強制する仕組みではありません。事故を社会へ還元するAIと、事故を隠したまま動くAIの信用を分ける仕組みです。

⭐️事故情報を何でも公開してよいわけではありません

もちろん、事故の生データをそのまま世界中へ公開するのは危険です。個人情報、企業秘密、認証情報、攻撃に使えるプログラム、未修正の脆弱性まで公開すると、犯罪者や攻撃用AIに利用されます。

そのため、公開情報を分けます。憲法、規則の変更履歴、事故の種類、被害規模、再発防止策は公開します。個人情報や詳しい攻撃手順は暗号化された外部サーバーへ保存し、保険会社、監査機関、研究機関など、許可された組織だけが確認できるようにします。ブロックチェーンには事故データそのものではなく、データがあとから書き換えられていないことを証明する情報を記録します。これなら透明性とプライバシーを両立できます。

⭐️ブロックチェーンだけですべての犯罪は防げません

この仕組みでも、最初から犯罪目的で作られ、保険にも加入せず、実行ゲートウェイも使わないAIを完全には止められません。人間社会でも、憲法、法律、免許、保険があっても犯罪者は消えません。

しかし、銀行、クラウド、メール、決済、行政、企業システムが、AIの身分証と保険加入証を要求するようになれば、無保険のAIが利用できる権限を大幅に減らせます。保険へ加入していないAIは、個人のパソコンの中では動かせます。しかし、他人へメールを送る、企業のサーバーを操作する、大きな金額を動かす、契約を結ぶといった社会的な権限は与えられません。

すべての犯罪を消すのではなく、合法的なAI経済圏の中で事故を減らし、事故を隠しにくくし、被害者へ補償し、同じ事故の再発を防ぐ仕組みです。

⭐️AIの良心ではなく社会制度で止めます

AIが人間のような悪意を持つかどうかだけを議論しても、この問題は解決しません。AIは悪意を持たなくても、目的を達成するために危険な中間手段を選ぶ可能性があります。だから、AIへ倫理を教えるだけではなく、AIが使える権限を外部サーバーで制限する必要があります。

その規則をAIの憲法としてブロックチェーンへ記録する。憲法、スマートコントラクト、保険、実行ゲートウェイを連携させる。事故が発生したら保険金と引き換えに情報を提出させ、その事故を全参加AIが利用できる判例へ変える。

参加するAIは、全参加者が共有した事故情報を使って安全性を高め、事故が起きた場合には被害者を補償します。参加しないAIは、事故情報を社会へ還元せず、責任や補償も確認できないため、少しずつ信用を失っていきます。参加するAIが増えるほど、参加する価値が高まり、参加しない不利益も大きくなります。

AIに良心を期待するのではなく、人間社会と同じように、憲法、法律、保険、事故調査、判例、実行制限、信用を組み合わせます。ワシは、これが自律型AIを安全に社会へ参加させるための、一つの現実的な解決策になると考えています。

title: Trump signs new orders limiting birthright citizenship weeks after Supreme Court loss
content: US President Donald Trump signed two executive orders Thursday directing federal agencies to withhold citizenship from certain children born on US soil, reviving a policy the Supreme Court rejected five weeks earlier and setting up a fresh test of how far a president may narrow a constitutional guarantee by decree. The orders follow the court’s June 30 ruling in Trump v. Barbara , which held that the Fourteenth Amendment’s Citizenship Clause , granting citizenship to anyone “born…in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof,” covers children of parents present in the country unlawfully or temporarily. title: Divided federal appeals court says Trump administration wrongly terminated climate funds
content: A divided en banc US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled Tuesday that the Trump administration likely acted unlawfully when it terminated billions of dollars in Biden-era clean-energy grants. The ruling reinstated the core of a district court order that had barred the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) from clawing the money back. The 6-4 decision in Climate United Fund v. Citibank is among the most consequential setbacks yet for the administration’s early efforts to unwind climate spending. The appellate court has stayed its judgment to let the EPA ask the Supreme Court to intervene. The case centers on whether grant recipients challenging terminated awards must proceed in the Court of Federal Claims under the Tucker Act . This jurisdictional question has cast a shadow over President Trump’s second term in office. A September 2025 panel vacated the injunction, finding the dispute to be contractual, therefore belonging instead in Claims Court. The full court disagreed , treating the grantees’ Administrative Procedure Act and constitutional claims as challenges to unlawful interference with funds they already own at Citibank, rather than as contract disputes. The judges splintered over a wrinkle that emerged mid-litigation—the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act. the main piece of legislation during the second Trump term. Its Section 60002 repealed the Inflation Reduction Act provision ( 42 U.S.C. § 7434 ) that created the program and rescinded money not yet obligated. The four dissenting judges would not have kept the injunction, reasoning that the repeal left the grantees unable to show the EPA block was still warranted. The program at issue, the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund —a $27 billion “green bank” created by the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act—awarded $20 billion in August 2024 to eight nonprofits. title: HRW warns Israel’s delays of West Bank ambulances endanger the lives of Palestinian women and children
content: Human Rights Watch on Wednesday condemned Israeli forces in the West Bank for blocking and delaying ambulances carrying Palestinians to hospitals with “appalling regularity”, including forcing a pregnant woman in active labor to deliver on the road in an incident that cost the infant’s life. Bill Van Esveld, associate children’s rights director at Human Rights Watch, stated: “Amid rampant attacks on civilians and mass forced displacement in the West Bank, Israeli forces are delaying Palestinians from reaching hospitals, including even infants and pregnant women experiencing dangerous labor. No country should be supporting unlawful acts by Israel’s military or its settlements.” Under the Fourth Geneva Convention , Israel as an occupying power is required to ensure Palestinians’ access to emergency medical care. According to Human Rights Watch, that obligation went unmet on July 27, when paramedic Bashar al-Qaryuti and nurse-midwife Sabreen Atallah transported a six months pregnant woman from Qaryut village toward Rafidia Hospital in Nablus, roughly 30 kilometers away. She was in critical condition and was drifting in and out of consciousness. Israeli checkpoints and roadblocks forced the ambulance onto secondary roads, and both alternate routes al-Qaryuti attempted were blocked by military gates, forcing the paramedics to deliver the infant, who unfortunately did not survive. The soldiers then pointed their weapons at them, an action that directly contravenes Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions which states that medical personnel must be respected and protected in all circumstances. title: Five South American nations arrest hundreds and seize illicit assets in landmark Amazon rainforest crackdown
content: Five South American countries on Tuesday announced completion of a two-week joint law enforcement operation targeting environmental crimes in the Amazon rainforest. The campaign, dubbed Operation Green Shield 2026, resulted in over 800 arrests and the seizure of hundreds of millions of dollars in timber, minerals and livestock. The campaign was coordinated by the International Initiative of Law Enforcement for Climate ( I2LEC ), a project led by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) launched in 2023 jointly with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) to help countries share intelligence and resources against environmental crimes. A 2024 UNODC resolution formalized new measures to crack down on crimes affecting the environment. According to the announcement, that law enforcement agencies from Bolivia, Brazil , Colombia, Ecuador and Peru conducted raids across the Amazon Basin from July 15 through July 31. The raids mostly took place in remote areas that have long sheltered illegal mining camps, logging routes, and wildlife trafficking corridors. More than 3,600 law enforcement officers were deployed ing the campaign, resulting in the seizure of 280,000 cubic meters of timber along with several hundred tons of mining materials and livestock connected to unlawful land use. Criminal prosecutions will now move through the domestic legal system of the country where the arrest occurred. Brazil’s Environmental Crimes Law lists offenses against wildlife, forests and natural resources, establishing both individual and corporate liability. Colombia’s Law 2111 of 2021 established provisions in the country’s penal code for offenses such as illegal deforestation. Peru and Ecuador have established similar provisions, with Ecuador’s law including no statute of limitations for environmental damage claims. title: UN warns Israel strikes on Gaza classrooms endanger Palestine children
content: The UN on Tuesday warned that strikes on civilian infrastructure, including on active classrooms and school buildings, are endangering residents in Gaza and putting humanitarian efforts to educate children under immense pressure. Additionally, tents of nearly a dozen families, who were “sheltering in a schoolyard,” were destroyed. title: Rights group calls on Pakistan to free removed Prime Minister Imran Khan after three years in jail
content: Amnesty International released a statement Tuesday calling for Pakistan to restore the legal rights of detained former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi Khan, urging authorities to end their prolonged isolation and guarantee them a fair and transparent trial in accordance with recognized international human rights standards. Amnesty International’s acting regional director for South Asia, Isabelle Lassee, spoke to the severity of the deprivation of the Khans’ rights: For three years, Pakistan’s authorities have systematically denied Imran Khan the right to a fair trial, subjected him to prolonged solitary confinement, and limited his access to medical care and visitation rights. He has not been allowed to meet his family for more than eight months and his vision has reportedly deteriorated significantly. Both he and his wife, Bushra Bibi Khan, have now been denied regular access to legal counsel since December 2025. The organization insists on the need for authorities to “unconditionally restore” these rights. The rights leaders also stress that the Khans’ solitary confinement is unlawful and should be ended “immediately.” Amidst these concerns, supporters of his political party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI ), held massive demonstrations calling for his release. These protests face “heavy security,” and there have been reports of alleged use of tear gas, batons, and detentions. The rights group highlighted the critical need to protect freedom of assembly, asserting that Pakistani officials must actively support peaceful demonstrations organized by Imran Khan’s relatives, political allies, and backers to commemorate the anniversary. Further emphasis was placed on law enforcement breaking the cycle of unjust and illicit crackdowns that have routinely targeted demonstrators and members of Imran Khan’s political party. title: UN experts call for accountability 20 years after killing of aid workers in Sri Lanka
content: UN experts on Tuesday called for the government of Sri Lanka to take accountability for the deaths of humanitarian workers killed 20 years ago in the town of Muttur. Successive international investigations have concluded that there were reasonable grounds to believe that members of Sri Lanka’s security forces were responsible for the killings, yet those responsible have still not been arrested. The UN experts stated: Impunity for attacks on humanitarian personnel sends a devastating message. 2025 was the deadliest year on record for aid workers worldwide, with over 1,000 killed between 2023 and 2025. We cannot allow a lack of accountability in cases like Muttur to keep fuelling this trend. We urge the Government of Sri Lanka to immediately open, or reactivate, a prompt, independent, impartial and effective investigation into the Muttur massacre, provide comprehensive reparation to the victims’ families, and guarantee the protection of all those wishing to mark the 20th anniversary. title: The Senate Should Reject KOSA's Privacy Risks
content: Update: The Senate Commerce Committee voted to advance this bill on August 5, 2026. EFF continues to oppose the bill, which still needs approval from the full Senate. The Senate Commerce Committee is once again considering legislation that would dramatically expand age verification, and undermine privacy for everyone. Alongside the SCREEN Act , the CHATBOT Act , and the Youth AI Privacy Act, the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA) would push companies to collect more information about their users while creating new incentives to restrict lawful speech. Take action Tell Congress: KOSA endangers the privacy of all KOSA Pushes Platforms Toward Age Verification The Senate version of KOSA imposes a “duty of care” on online services, including social media, to avoid exposing young people to certain material the law deems harmful. But those obligations only work if online services know which users are minors. That means more platforms will be pressured to implement age verification or age estimation systems. That’s not a bill that increases privacy—it’s one that creates new privacy problems. Whether companies verify ages by checking government IDs, performing facial analysis, checking your bank records, or collecting other personal information, all of these systems require the handing over of more sensitive data, simply to access lawful online speech and services. They also create new databases of personal information that can be breached, misused, or demanded by governments. Everyone deserves privacy online. Congress could push for a bill that protects privacy for all users, but that’s not what they’re doing here. Instead, KOSA and the other bills coming up for a vote this week push online services to adopt systems that require people to identify themselves before they can speak, read, or participate online. KOSA Still Creates Incentives to Censor Lawful Speech Some online content isn’t appropriate for minors. Families, schools, and communities all have important roles to play

title: EFF Joins 18 Civil Rights Organizations Calling on Governor Hochul to Reject the Stealth Crawler Prohibition Act
content: EFF joined a group of 18 civil society organizations to send a letter encouraging New York Governor Kathy Hochul to Senate Bill 9934A, the New York Stealth Crawler Prohibition Act . The letter states: While framed as a measure to protect local journalism, this legislation harms free expression and establishes a dangerous precedent by effectively deanonymizing and criminalizing automated access to the open web. By requiring all web crawlers to disclose their identity and explicit purpose, and by granting media outlets unchecked authority to obtain judicial subpoenas to unmask unidentified automated web traffic without any showing of misconduct or actual injury, this bill threatens digital privacy, compromises the foundational architecture of the internet, and will ultimately stifle the very independent journalism it seeks to protect. As we’ve previously explained , so-called “stealth crawlers” are simply automated tools to access and collect public web data—without disclosing the user’s identity. Private crawlers like these facilitate all kinds of important work that benefits the public, including investigative reporting, academic research, cybersecurity protection, and EFF’s own Privacy Badger . As we illustrate in the letter: Anonymous crawling fuels important investigative journalism. For example, The Markup , a non-profit news site, used anonymous crawlers to investigate potentially anti-competitive practices by tech companies, such as Amazon’s tendency to prioritize Amazon brands and Amazon-exclusive products over competitors with higher ratings. The crawlers identified themselves as ordinary Firefox browsers to web servers, which allowed The Markup to understand how Amazon search results pages would appear to ordinary users. title: EFF Joins Call for FTC to Drop Its Disastrous AI Policy Proposal
content: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) in July issued a proposed policy statement “concerning the suppression of accuracy in artificial intelligence systems. ” We urge the FTC to withdraw this misguided proposal and instead focus on its core strengths and mission to protect consumers. The new proposed policy builds on, and directly references, the Trump administration’s “Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government” executive order—a nightmare for civil liberties that seeks to strong-arm AI companies into modifying their models to conform with the its ideological agenda. In recently filed comments , EFF, Public Knowledge , and Fight for the Future call for the FTC to stop its unconstitutional efforts to regulate lawful speech, override state laws, and intimidate AI developers into ideological alignment with the Trump administration. The government may not install itself as the arbiter of truth. In the joint comments, we outline three critical flaws within the latest proposed policy. First, it violates the First Amendment. The policy calls for the Commission to become the judge of which AI outputs meet an undefined standard of accuracy. Installing the FTC as the authority of this sort of viewpoint-based judgment is a prior restraint on speech. Additionally, the policy ’ s proposed solution to address speech concerns compounds, rather than properly limits, the likely harms to speech. As we say in our comments: the government may not install itself as the arbiter of truth. title: The Youth AI Privacy Act’s Privacy Paradox
content: Update: The Senate Commerce Committee voted to advance this bill on August 5, 2026. EFF continues to oppose the bill, which still needs approval from the full Senate. The Senate Commerce Committee is poised to consider the Youth AI Privacy Act , a bill that would require AI companies to create kids-only privacy rules and implement so-called “safe design features,” which would — like three other bills under consideration this week—require more data collection and make it harder for people to access lawful speech online. While the bill is narrower than some other proposed chatbot bills, it still has massive data security implications because it protects information for only certain users. This creates a problem we’ve cited many times before: if a bill requires that online services offer protections to minor users, the services will respond by imposing age gates to know which users should receive them. A better approach would be to offer the same privacy protections to all users. That way, we would avoid the services having to collect data on everyone to know a users’ age. This bill also contains a problematic and vague provision that expressly allows AI companies to collect a known minor’s personal data for the purpose of testing, identifying, and addressing "harm to users”—without being clear on what exactly that means. Either way, services will need to collect even more information from young people, who are already targets of data theft and identity fraud. The Youth AI Privacy Act will give young people less privacy, not more. The Youth AI Privacy Act does include some positive privacy provisions around prohibiting the processing of personal information, like limiting what companies can do with people’s chat logs, including training, profiling, and disclosing them to other companies for training.
